theme: At the Feast of Booths; the woman caught in adultery
readingInstruction: Read John 7:1-8:11. Jesus teaches at the Feast of Booths amid confusion about who he is, and then a woman caught in adultery is brought to him. A note: the story in 7:53-8:11 is not found in the earliest manuscripts, and many translations set it apart. It is widely accepted as an authentic account of Jesus, though scholars differ on whether John wrote it.
settingTheScene: The Feast of Booths was a joyful autumn festival that remembered the wilderness wanderings. Each day a priest drew water from the pool of Siloam and poured it at the altar, and lamps lit up the temple courts. Against this background, Jesus stands on the last and greatest day and offers living water. The crowd is divided. The leaders are looking for a way to arrest him.
observation: “If anyone’s will is to do God’s will, he will know whether the teaching is from God or whether I am speaking on my own authority” (7:17).
“So they were seeking to arrest him, but no one laid a hand on him, because his hour had not yet come” (7:30).
“If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink” (7:37).
“Whoever believes in me, as the Scripture has said, Out of his heart will flow rivers of living water” (7:38).
“No one ever spoke like this man!” (7:46).
“Let him who is without sin among you be the first to throw a stone at her” (8:7).
“Woman, where are they? Has no one condemned you?” (8:10).
“Neither do I condemn you; go, and from now on sin no more” (8:11).
interpretation:
Jesus’ brothers urge him to go to Judea and show himself, but they do not believe in him. He says his time has not yet come, and goes up privately. At the feast, people debate. Some say he is a good man; others say he is leading the people astray. In the middle of the feast, he teaches in the temple. “My teaching is not mine, but his who sent me.” And he gives a principle for judging truth: if anyone is willing to do God’s will, he will know.

On the last day of the feast, when the water ceremony had ended, Jesus cries out, “If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink.” John explains that he spoke about the Spirit, whom believers would receive after Jesus was glorified. The temple guards come back empty-handed, saying, “No one ever spoke like this man!” Nicodemus, who first came by night, speaks up for fairness.

Then the scene changes. The scribes and Pharisees bring a woman caught in adultery and set her before Jesus, quoting the law of Moses that she should be stoned. It is a trap: if he says to release her, he disregards the law, and if he says to stone her, he loses his reputation for mercy and contradicts Roman law. Jesus stoops and writes on the ground. When they keep asking, he says, “Let him who is without sin among you be the first to throw a stone at her.” One by one, beginning with the oldest, they go away. Jesus is left alone with the woman. “Has no one condemned you?” “No one, Lord.” “Neither do I condemn you; go, and from now on sin no more.”

Notice the order. Jesus does not say, “Go and sin no more, and then I will not condemn you.” He says he does not condemn, and then calls her to a new life. Grace comes first and makes obedience possible. And Jesus can say this because he is the one who will bear her condemnation on the cross.
connection: Leviticus 23:33-43 describes the Feast of Booths. Isaiah 12:3 and Zechariah 14:8, 16-19 connect living water and the feast to the age to come. Isaiah 44:3 promises the Spirit poured out on the thirsty. Deuteronomy 17:6-7 and Leviticus 20:10 relate to the case of adultery. Romans 8:1 says there is now no condemnation for those in Christ Jesus. Romans 3:23-24 says all have sinned and are justified by grace. Hebrews 4:15-16 speaks of our sympathetic high priest.
application:
If you are thirsty, go to Jesus and drink. Tell him what you are thirsting for.

Put down any stones you are holding against others. Remember your own sin.

Hear “Neither do I condemn you” as spoken to you, and then ask what “go and sin no more” looks like for you today.
prayerPrompts: Come to Jesus thirsty, and tell him what you thirst for.
Ask him to pour out his Spirit like rivers of living water.
Thank him for his compassion for the woman caught in sin.
